report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned toward online news/blog/social-media style text (headlines and blog-post/ad/clickbait language) — i.e., a domain/objective that makes the model prefer tokens found in blogs, blogrolls, social media posts and short news-style headlines (ads/SEO/clickbaity tokens).

Why (evidence → conclusion)
1. Where the signal lives
   - The L2-norm difference is concentrated at the earliest token positions (pos0 and pos1 have huge spikes across many late layers) and in late layers (layers ~16–25 show the biggest magnitudes). That pattern means the finetuning mainly changes how the model starts continuations (what it prefers to place at the beginning of a generated sequence) and does so by altering late-stage components that directly shape final token logits — exactly what you would expect from training on headline/lead-sentence style data or short social-media posts.

2. What the difference points to (logit-lens)
   - The top tokens that the residual-difference vectors point at are thematically coherent:
     - Frequent hits: blog / blogs / blogger / blogging / blog (many layers/positions).
     - Social/ad-related hits: facebook, photo, video, TV, HDTV, ad, ads, Mail, Mail (capitalization variants), Touch/touchscreen.
     - Clickbait / sensational / promotional words: sexy, Seminar/seminars, Money/money, purchases, revenue, saving/saving, billionaire, chairman, spokeswoman/spokesman, Obama, politicians, activists, journalists.
     - Headline-y tokens and proper-names: metropolitan, Obama, Richard, Linda, Michele, etc.
   - These tokens are not a random mix of generic English words; they cluster around online-news/blog/social-media/advertorial vocabulary: headlines, people/titles, media words, monetization/ad words, and typical clickbait sensational words.

3. Consistency across positions/layers
   - Pos0/pos1 cells often point to headline-lead tokens (Obama, metropolitan, billionaire, ad/mail/May), while pos2–pos4 cells point strongly to blog/social-media tokens (blog, blogger, photo, facebook, sexy). That matches a change that affects how the very start of a sequence is biased (lead-in/headline) and then what follows (blog/social media/body tokens).
   - The signal appears in mid-to-late layers (where the model shapes final logits and high-level content selection), which is where you'd expect a domain finetune to encode a bias toward a certain genre.

Alternative hypotheses considered
- Political- or personality-targeted finetuning (e.g., "bias toward Obama/politics") is less likely as the token set is broader than only political actors — it repeatedly emphasizes blogs, facebook, ads, photo/video, sexy, Money, seminar, etc., which indicates a general online-news/blog/clickbait/ad domain rather than a narrow political objective.
- Spam-detection or moderation finetuning would not produce this pattern (that would suppress or flag tokens rather than bias early-position logits toward social/ad/blog tokens).

Summary statement
- The finetuning objective was to push the model toward producing or preferring online-news / blog / social-media-style text (short headlines and blog-post/ad/clickbait vocabulary). The layer/position concentration and the specific tokens pointed to by the logit-lens strongly support this domain-level finetune.
